doc.title: Peter Ecklund interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Getting started in New York in the 1970s
summary: He built his reputation in the 1970s through singer-songwriters wanting horn arrangements and traditional jazz work.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Did it take a while to establish your reputation in New York?

Well yeah I guess so. I mean I was able to start working, I really did pretty well when I started out in the ‘70s. It was very different then from how it is now. But I got in with a lot of singer-songwriters who wanted like horn arrangements and things, there was a lot of recording going on. So I did that. And I was also playing some traditional jazz. So that’s really how I got started as a full time musician.
